extracted.intended_audience: local journalists, newsroom leaders, and community-focused journalism funders
extracted.subtask_description: A framework for evaluating and producing local news that centers community needs, builds trust, and prioritizes practical, locally relevant, and solutions-oriented coverage. Intended to guide newsroom decisions about what to cover and how to engage communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core principle: Ground work in community need
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ground work in community need, not your own. The best way to earn community support is to focus on serving and solving community needs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage decisions should start from identified community needs rather than newsroom agendas; earning support comes from service and problem-solving orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responds to identified community need
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage responds to needs surfaced through listening; listening informs coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use community input (listening sessions, advisory boards, pitches) to pick and shape stories. Stories should address issues the community has identified as important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practically useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Information the audience can act on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting that provides actionable information (how-to, resources, steps residents can take) rather than abstraction or pure analysis with no clear utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Affects this specific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on impacts and contexts that matter to the local population; avoid treating national narratives as local news when local specifics exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions-oriented
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that highlights responses and potential solutions, not only problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reporting on what is working, reform efforts, policy responses, and community-driven fixes; avoid purely problem-centric stories without exploring remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voices of community members centered
rubrics_metrics.description: Center community members' perspectives rather than treating them merely as sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevate lived experience, firsthand accounts, and community expertise; frame residents as participants, not just providers of quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize underserved communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Give coverage priority to communities that are undercovered or marginalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentionally seek out stories, sources, and issues from underserved groups to correct coverage imbalances and better serve community needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust-building: Builds rather than burns
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice journalism that builds trust with community members rather than eroding it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether reporting decisions, framing, and engagement strengthen relationships with audiences; avoid sensationalism and practices that alienate readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic engagement enabling
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that enables or encourages civic participation and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report in ways that inform voters, help residents participate in civic processes, and make public affairs more navigable and actionable for the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom acts as community member
rubrics_metrics.description: The newsroom behaves as part of the community, going beyond traditional detached boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show up at events, participate in community life in appropriate roles, and treat the newsroom as accountable to community members rather than as an external observer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview community as customers, not sources — structured conversations to surface needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use listening sessions to understand priorities, concerns, and information gaps; design coverage based on those findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch Days
rubrics_metrics.description: Community presents needs to journalism funders or newsrooms through structured pitch events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold opportunities for residents and community groups to propose reporting ideas tied to local needs; use these to align funding and editorial priorities with community demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community advisory boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal or semi-formal groups that advise newsroom decisions and priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advisory boards to provide ongoing feedback, represent diverse perspectives, and hold the newsroom accountable to community standards and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions reporting (as a trust-building method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on what is working in the community — evidence-backed responses to problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt methods from Solutions Journalism Network: rigorous reporting on responses, outcomes, and lessons rather than uncritical boosterism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about process
rubrics_metrics.description: Be open about reporting methods, decision-making, and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how stories are reported, what information was available, and where uncertainties remain to build credibility and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging journalism's mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly recognize and correct errors or missteps in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid, visible corrections and accountability practices help maintain and rebuild trust when coverage harms or misrepresents community members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing up at community events outside reporter role
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend local gatherings in roles beyond reporting to build relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in community life (with appropriate boundaries) to better understand context and demonstrate commitment; not only parachute in to cover a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as news: Issues raised in community listening
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories identified through listening exercises should be considered newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let community-raised issues guide news agendas rather than solely newsroom-driven beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as news: Practical concerns of residents
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyday practical issues (services, housing, schools, transit) are newsworthy when they affect residents' lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight reporting that addresses immediate, day-to-day problems people face and provide useful information or solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as news: Solutions to local problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on local solutions and responses is newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature stories that document successful interventions, experiments, or community initiatives with replicable lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as news: Stories of resilience and agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Narratives that showcase community resilience, agency, and capacity are valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories that foreground how residents respond, adapt, and organize rather than only portraying them as victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as news: Voices not previously heard
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring forward perspectives and communities that have been excluded or ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively seek and amplify underrepresented voices to broaden civic conversation and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as news: Bridging across community divides
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that connects different parts of the community and fosters understanding is newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support reporting that builds common ground and addresses polarization by explaining diverse viewpoints and shared interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devalued: National-press-driven stories over local issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories driven primarily by national press themes are devalued when local issues exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid forcing national narratives onto local coverage when there are more relevant local matters to pursue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devalued: Crime over-coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive focus on crime is discouraged when it crowds out other community priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce sensational, disproportionate crime coverage that distorts community realities and erodes trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devalued: Helicopter journalism (parachute in/out)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term, extractive reporting that comes in and leaves without relationship-building is devalued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'parachuting' into communities; favor sustained engagement and accountability to residents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devalued: Engagement-bait
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories designed primarily to drive clicks or engagement metrics rather than serve community needs are devalued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject attention-seeking tactics that prioritize metrics over public service and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devalued: Negativity for negativity's sake
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that is negative without public-service value is devalued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not default to negative framing when it does not illuminate solutions, context, or public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer sustained coverage with community over episodic crisis coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Community-centered practice favors ongoing, sustained reporting in partnership with the community rather than episodic crisis-driven stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop long-term reporting projects that follow issues over time, integrating community feedback and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize civic need, solutions, and voice over conflict/prominence/drama
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike traditional newsworthiness (which often centers conflict and prominence), community-centered criteria prioritize civic need, solutions, and community voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reorient editorial judgment to value civic utility and representational equity instead of simply prominence or sensational conflict.
